Commentary.Commentary: Right then! The target for Afghanistan is 260 runs in their 50 overs. The pitch has slowed down considerably and the slower balls are doing wonder. Ireland would hope to bowl well and get over the line this time. Join us for the chase in a short while.

Afghanistan started well with the ball as Mujeeb got the wickets of Kevin O'Brien and Andy Balbirnie in his first two overs. They allowed Stirling to play his natural game. Nabi was excellent in his spell but could not eke out a wicket. Naveen-Ul-Haq was the pick of the bowlers with 4 wickets to his name while Mujeeb got three. Their efforts in the last 10 overs managed them to restrict Ireland to 259 or else they would have been chasing a big score.

Ireland got off to the worst possible start as they lost two wickets in the first 4 overs. But Paul Stiring had other ideas. He was aggressive right from the start and was involved in a good 84-run stand with Harry Tector for the third wicket. In process, he completed his 11th ODI ton. Curtis Campher supported Stirling as both of them took on the spinners with some lovely shots to bring up their 100-run stand. The former though was out just 3 short of his half ton. Stirling continued on his merry way and was finally dismissed by Naveen for 128. The lower order batters could not get going and lost wickets in the last 10. But they would be still happy with 259 on the board.

Ireland finish on a good score of 259 runs courtesy a brilliant ton from Paul Stirling. The Afghans will rue the fact that they could not capitalize on a good start and allowed Ireland to dictate the terms throughout the innings before making a late comeback.

NOT OUT! Missing the stumps! A good review from Ireland as it looked out to the naked eye. DRINKS! A brilliant start for Afghanistan after being asked to bowl. Mujeeb Ur Rahman once again struck in his first two overs to peg Ireland on the back foot but a good solid stand between Stirling and Tector has revived them back as Stirling went past his 25th ODI fifty. Ireland would want him to continue as others would look to play around him. Afghanistan on the other hand would want to see the back of the Irish opener as quickly as possible as they are aware of his heroics and once he gets going he is hard to stop. When will Afghanistan unleash Rashid Khan at the Ireland batsmen is the question now as these batsmen Tector and Stirling have settled down quite nicely.

FOUR! SHOT! A full ball outside off, Stirling creams this one through the cover-point area for a boundary. Stirling continues on his merry way despite losing partners from the other end.
Tossed up on off, pushed to covers by Tector. A good over from Mujeeb Ur Rahman.
Harry Tector is the new batsman at number 4.

Review time. Balbirnie has been given out LBW. He has taken it upstairs. Replays are in.. Its a fair delivery. Waiting for UltraEdge... Some issues here with UltraEdge. Finally no bat involved in UltraEdge. Ball Tracking shows Three Reds. Balbirnie has to go.

OUT! LBW! THREE REDS! Andy Balbirnie departs and so takes the review with him too. Mujeeb strikes again in his second over. Tossed up ball around off, spinning into Balbirnie who lines up to play the sweep. He though misses to get rapped on the pads. There comes the appeal from the Afghan players and the umpire raises his finger. Balbirnie after consulting his partner takes the review. Replays roll in and there comes the Ultra Edge. Nothing on it when the ball is near the bat. Ball Tracker comes in and shows Three Reds. Balbirnie has to depart.
Tossed up on off, pushed back to the bowler by Balbirnie.
Tossed up on off, pushed to the off side.
Floated on leg, Stirling turns it behind square leg and gets to the other end.
Tossed up on leg, tucked towards the leg side.
Good length and around off, Balbirnie plays it to covers off the back foot.
Length and around off, Andy plays it to covers.
FOUR! Slapped! Shorter and outside off, Balbirnie stands tall and cuts it through cover-point as the ball races to the fence behind.
Andy plays it towards cover-point off the back foot.
Good length and outside off, Balbirnie makes a leave this time.
Short of good length around off, Andy punches it towards point.
FOUR! Pulled away! Flatter and around off, Stirling rocks on the back foot and then pulls it through mid-wicket for another boundary.
FOUR! Creamed! Full and around off, Stirling comes on the front foot and then drives it through covers for another boundary. Stirling is in top form here.
Full on off, pushed wide of mid off for a single by Balbirnie.
Skipper Andrew Balbirnie walks in next.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Mujeeb strikes! Another failure for Kevin O'Brien. Mujeeb Ur Rahman tosses one up around off, O'Brien looks to play it off the back foot but the ball just about spins away taking the outside edge and settling into the hands of the first slip fielder where Gulbadin Naib takes the catch.
Floated ball around middle, Stirling clips it to mid-wicket for another single.
Tossed up ball on middle, O'Brien tucks it to mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single.
Who will bowl from the other end? Spin early with Mujeeb Ur Rahman.
FOUR! Glorious drive! Stirling and Ireland are underway! Slightly overpitched around off, Paul leans into the drive and creams it through covers as the ball races to the fence in no time.
Slightly fuller in length and around off, Stirling pushes it to point off the front foot.
Good length and on off, Stirling drives it but can only manage to get it to the man at mid on.
On a length and around off, Stirling makes a leave once again. The ball shows inward movement once it passed the batsman.
Good length and outside off, Stirling has no problems in leaving this one.
Signs of low bounce early on! Length and outside off, Stirling goes for a swat through the off side but the ball goes under his bat low to the keeper.

We are all set to begin. The Afghanistan players are on the field followed by the two Ireland openers, Paul Stirling and Kevin O'Brien. Naveen-Ul-Haq to start with the new ball for Afghanistan. Before the start of the game, players from both the teams observed two minutes silence for Najib Tarakai who passed away in 2020.
Afghanistan skipper, Asghar Afghan says he wanted to bowl first. Praises Gurbaz for his century in the last match. Also mentions that Shahidi replaces Omarzai.

Ireland skipper, Andy Balbirnie says it is use wicket so want runs on the boards. Admits that they were rusty the last match and would like to improve today. Praises McBrine for his 5-fer in the last match.
Pitch Report- The pitch has no grass whatsoever and it is rock hard. Both teams would love to bat first. Beautiful conditions for a good cricket match.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Javed Ahmadi, Rahmat Shah, Asghar Afghan (C), Hashmatullah Shahidi (IN FOR Azmatullah Omarzai), Mohammad Nabi, Najibullah Zadran, Gulbadin Naib, Rashid Khan, Naveen-ul-Haq, Mujeeb Ur Rahman.

Ireland (Unchanged Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Kevin O Brien, Andrew Balbirnie (C), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Simi Singh, Gareth Delany, Andy McBrine, Barry McCarthy, Craig Young.
It's time for toss as Afghanistan skipper, Asghar Afghan and Ireland skipper, Andy Balbirnie are out in the middle. Up she goes and lands in favour of Andy Balbirnie. IRELAND OPT OT BAT FIRST!

What an engrossing and an enthralling game we have had in the 1st ODI between Afghanistan and Ireland. Afghanistan edged out the Irish men by a mere 16 runs in the first game and now we are back again with the 2nd ODI. Hello and welcome for its coverage. First ODI saw a few heroes from both the teams in the form of Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Rashid Khan, Andy McBrine and Lorcan Tucker and this fight could spice up as we head to the game two. The Afghans would be worried of the Irish fightback and would want their star bowler Rashid Khan to come good with the ball. Irish on the other hand would hope to cross the line this time around. A cracking contest coming up as the toss and team updates coming up in a short while.
